sections.h2: Who bills property tax for a Greensboro home?
sections.html:
Guilford County bills it. Greensboro's city tax and the county tax come on one bill from the Guilford County Tax Department, which has offices at 400 W. Market St. in Greensboro and 325 E. Russell Ave. in High Point, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays.

For assessment and appeal questions call 336-641-4814. For payment questions the county's FAQ gives 336-641-3363 as the line to call about a payment arrangement. The city sets its own rate, and the county's rate page lists it as a separate line.

If your lender escrows taxes, it will ask the county for the bill. The county notes that state law still makes the owner responsible for seeing that taxes are paid, so check the notice you receive in July and forward it to the correct servicer if the company named is not the one holding your escrow.

sections.h2: What property tax rates apply inside Greensboro?
sections.html:
The county's 2026-2027 rate page prints a countywide rate of 0.78950 and a City of Greensboro rate of 0.79850, for a total of 1.58800 under rate code 01. Rates are expressed as a fraction of $1 per $100 of assessed value.

sections.h2: How did Senate Bill 889 change Greensboro property tax bills?
sections.html:
It froze the use of the 2026 reappraisal values for one year, so bills for the fiscal year that began July 1, 2026 rest on the older values. The City of Greensboro says the moratorium applies to the county's revaluation process and does not stop local governments from changing their rates.

  • Greensboro adopted its fiscal year 2026-27 budget on June 16, with a total city rate of 79.85 cents.
  • The city describes that as a 12.6-cent adjustment on current property values, not on the new reappraisal values.
  • The county says the updated values are paused until January 1, 2027, and are expected to feed the budget year that begins July 1, 2027.

The practical result: your new notice of value does not set this year's bill. It still matters, because if the value is wrong, the appeal clock runs on it, and an appeal that stays open now is considered for the 2027 tax year.

sections.h2: When are Greensboro property taxes due, and how can I pay?
sections.html:
Taxes are due September 1 and go delinquent after January 5. Under G.S. 105-360 a bill paid by January 5 carries no interest, and Guilford County's FAQ says interest runs at 2% for the first month and 0.75% added on the first day of each month after.

  • Discount: the county rate page says Guilford County and Greensboro offer a 1.0% discount for payment before September 1.
  • Online or by phone at (336) 203-7795: an electronic processing fee of 1.85% plus a $2 transaction fee.
  • In person at either tax office: cash or check, or card with a 2.35% over-the-counter fee plus $2.
  • By mail: Guilford County Tax Department, P.O. Box 70939, Charlotte, NC 28272-0939.

A mailed payment counts on the date of the U.S. Postal Service postmark, and the burden of proof that it was timely rests on the taxpayer. The county says it will never call and ask for payment unless a bill is delinquent, and that bills cannot be paid with gift cards.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Greensboro property value?
sections.html:
File an appeal with the Guilford County Tax Department. For tax year 2026 the county says appeals may be submitted through December 31, 2026, and for tax year 2027 they may be filed through May 17, 2027, with the online portal opening January 1, 2027.

Anyone who already appealed the reappraisal value keeps that appeal active, and it will be considered for 2027 with no new filing. Before the moratorium the county's published deadline was May 15, 2026, at 5 p.m.

For a paper appeal, the county suggests handing it to a USPS clerk and asking for a hand-cancelled postmark, because a mailbox drop may be postmarked a day later and carries no proof of date. Appeals postmarked after May 17 are not accepted. To ask for a form before the portal opens, email taxreval@guilfordcountync.gov.

The Board of Equalization and Review hears appeals the staff cannot resolve, and a further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission within 30 days after the board mails its decision (G.S. 105-290). Personal property values are a separate matter: appeals of value, situs and taxability must be filed within 30 days of the notice date.

sections.h2: What tax relief can Greensboro homeowners apply for?
sections.html:
Three state programs are open to homeowners in Greensboro, and the application deadline is June 1 each year. Applications go to the Guilford County Tax Department, PO Box 3138, Greensboro, NC 27402, or by hand to either tax office.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of value, for owners 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, with gross income not over $38,800 as the county prints it. The owner applies once.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: taxes held to 4% or 5% of income, with income caps of $38,800 and $58,200 as printed. The owner must have lived in the home five years and apply every year.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 off appraised value, no age or income limit, and a single application.

An owner can use only one program. After June 1, the county evaluates late applications up to one week before the last Board of Equalization and Review meeting in December. Call 336-641-3320 or 336-641-7911 with questions. If a circuit breaker owner sells, the last three years of deferred tax become payable with interest on the date of the sale.

sections.h2: What happens when Greensboro property tax goes unpaid before a sale?
sections.html:
Interest starts and the county begins enforced collection, and the tax stays a lien on the parcel. The county lists garnishment of wages and bank accounts, levy on personal property, attachment of state refunds and lottery winnings, and foreclosure on real estate.

The lien attaches as of the listing date under G.S. 105-355, with penalties and costs. A court foreclosure ends in an auction at the courthouse door under G.S. 105-374, and the owner can redeem before confirmation by paying the taxes, interest, penalties and costs. The Guilford County Tax Department says it does not conduct tax lien sales.

If you plan to sell, request the payoff figures for the current bill before you list. Any deferred tax from a relief program is separate and has to be asked for by name.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Greensboro?
sections.html:
Greensboro had 308,667 residents on July 1, 2025, up from 299,035 at the 2020 Census and 269,666 in 2010. The city covers about 130 square miles of land at roughly 2,308 people per square mile.

  • Households: 123,984 for 2020 to 2024, averaging 2.29 people.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 50.5%.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $244,800.
  • Median gross rent: $1,172.
  • Median household income: $61,515.
  • Mean travel time to work: 21.7 minutes.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher: 41.0%.

Renters and owners are about even, so a sale in Greensboro often involves a landlord or an investor on one side. Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $1,447, a figure worth comparing with the tax bill on any house you own.

faqs.q: Who sends the Greensboro property tax bill?
faqs.a: Guilford County. The county tax department bills the county and city tax together, and its offices are at 400 W. Market St., Greensboro, and 325 E. Russell Ave., High Point.

faqs.q: What is the Greensboro property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county's 2026-2027 table prints 0.78950 countywide and 0.79850 for the City of Greensboro, a total of 1.58800 for rate code 01. Historic and downtown districts add a separate charge.

faqs.q: Is there an early payment discount in Greensboro?
faqs.a: Yes. The county rate page says Guilford County and Greensboro offer a 1.0% discount for payment before September 1. After January 5 interest applies.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Greensboro property value after the moratorium?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says 2026 appeals may be submitted through December 31, 2026, and 2027 appeals through May 17, 2027, with the online portal opening January 1, 2027. An earlier appeal stays active.

faqs.q: Does Guilford County sell tax liens?
faqs.a: No. The county tax department says it does not conduct tax lien sales, but it does enforce collection through measures that include garnishment and foreclosure on real estate.
